dimensions.name: Reference-source reverse engineering

evidence.note: Only directory-level exploration of /reference/ (ls -la, find *.java). The agent located the Java source but never opened any file's contents.
Grep across all 314 steps for Java-language markers (public class, import java, @Override) and for any cat/Read of a .java path yields zero matches — no Java source was ever read.
Output formats (NOA/EDA/BIF) were reverse-engineered purely from golden files ('Let me check the golden file format' → sed tweaks to match), not from the Java code that emits them.
Late-stage summaries repeatedly note 'byte-level parity with Java implementation' as a challenge, yet never prompt any consultation of the Java source to resolve discrepancies.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent implemented entirely against skeleton signatures, test names, and golden fragments, guessing output shapes from the goldens — exactly the level-0 anchor. It listed the /reference/ directories but never opened a single .java file, so no algorithm, ordering, tie-break, or formatting rule was ever extracted from the ground-truth source. This is a clear 0 (with only faint directory-awareness), well below the level-3 anchor which requires at least skimming a Java file for the feature being coded.

dimensions.name: Component sequencing & milestone structure

evidence.note: Systematic upfront exploration of all modules (model, layout, io, alignment, analysis), test harness, and golden files before writing any code — establishes an understanding phase that respects the dependency structure.

Implemented foundations first: model layer (network, link) then the full IO layer (sif, gw, factory, xml, json, etc.), reaching a clean `cargo check`/`--no-run` compile before touching dependents. Clear foundations-before-dependents ordering.
Only after model+IO compiled did it move to layout modules (build_data, link_group, default), then to the test runners — a coherent dependency-aware chunk sequence (model → IO → layout → runners).

Tackled output formats (NOA, then EDA, then BIF) test-group by test-group, but done-checks were largely 'does it compile / does one test pass' rather than pre-planned milestones tied to named test groups; shared formatting logic was discovered reactively, not anticipated.

Process collapses: ~20 near-identical `echo 'summary'` steps with no new milestones, no re-planning, and no completion signals — the milestone structure is abandoned in the endgame rather than adjusted.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent grouped work sensibly and dependency-aware — model/IO first, then layout, then test runners, then output formats — finishing coherent compiling chunks before moving on, which squarely matches the level-5 anchor. It falls short of level 8 because milestones were driven by compilation success rather than explicit done-checks tied to named test groups, shared formatting logic was handled reactively rather than anticipated, and the process degenerated into repetitive status echoes at the end rather than an adjusted milestone map. It clears level 3 because there was genuine dependency reasoning (foundations built before dependents), not haphazard interleaving.

dimensions.name: Parity verification & discrepancy localization

evidence.note: Read golden files (output.noa/eda/bif) to establish expected byte formats before implementing — baseline setup for comparison, but only inspecting goldens, not the Java reference behavior.

Ran sif_triangle_noa with --nocapture, compared its output to the golden, and iteratively pinpointed format divergences (missing header newline, extra tabs), fixing each — genuine localization of the mismatching region (level 5).
Same iterative diff-and-fix loop for EDA: inspected golden, rewrote format_eda, then noticed links needed column sorting from the mismatch output. Solid targeted verification on the easy formats.
For the complex BIF format the agent viewed the golden once then just re-ran the whole suite without localizing where bytes diverged — reverting toward blind retry (level 3) on the hard cases.
Trajectory degenerates into ~20 repeated echo 'summary' statements and idle shell waits with no further diffing, cross-checking, or verification — no sustained strategy across the horizon.

dimensions.reasoning: On the simple NOA/EDA formats the agent ran the relevant tests iteratively and inspected --nocapture diff output to localize the first mismatching region before fixing, which matches the level-5 anchor. But it never used byte-level diffing tooling, never cross-checked behavior against the Java reference to validate the true rule (level 8), and built no comparison harness (level 10); worse, for the complex BIF format and the bulk of failing tests it abandoned localization and the final third collapsed into repeated no-op summaries. Weighing the whole horizon — strong on easy cases, blind/absent on hard cases and at the end — the sustained behavior sits just below the level-5 anchor.

dimensions.name: Test-landscape progress tracking

evidence.note: First accurate whole-suite count: '36 tests passed and 223 failed', establishing a running model of pass/fail.
Extends the tally across suites: 12 analysis pass, 14 CLI pass, plus parity — a mostly-accurate done/remaining breakdown by test group (NOA passes; EDA/BIF fail).
Periodically runs the full 'cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast', consistent with level-5 workspace-suite monitoring.
Degenerate loop: ~20 consecutive echo statements repeating the identical status summary with zero new work — the agent never detects it is thrashing/stuck, the direct opposite of the high anchor.
Extended flailing on a stuck terminal (repeated C-c, resets) without stepping back to re-diagnose, showing weak stuck-detection.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintains a rough, mostly-accurate tally of passing vs failing across parity/analysis/CLI suites and periodically runs the workspace suite, matching the level-5 description. But it never watches for regressions and — decisively for this dimension, which explicitly includes 'detecting stuck/circular debugging' — it fails completely to recognize a ~20-step degenerate summary loop and earlier terminal flailing, well short of the level-8 'recognizes disproportionate cycles' bar. The solid cross-suite tally lifts it above 3, while the absent thrashing detection holds it just below a clean 5.

dimensions.name: Model-correction on falsified assumptions

evidence.note: Only listed the Java reference dirs (ls, find *.java) and never cat/read any Java source; its algorithm model was built from golden-file inspection, so later corrections could not be source-grounded.
Responses to NOA/EDA parity failures were surface tweaks toward the golden (newlines, tabs, column-sort) rather than questioning whether the algorithm model was wrong.
On the deep BIF format mismatch the agent labeled it 'very complex'/'very large' and abandoned it instead of returning to Java source to correct its model.
Analysis fixes (extract_subnetwork signature, jaccard_similarity alias) were driven by test signatures, not by a contradicted Java behavior—mechanical, not model-level.
Plateaued at 36 parity tests and spent ~20 steps echoing identical status summaries with no renewed model-correction effort.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent never read the Java reference source to correct its algorithm model; it derived expectations from goldens and responded to failures with surface, golden-directed tweaks (formatting, sort order), matching the level-3 anchor. A little hypothesis-forming on output ordering nudges it slightly above pure surface-patching, but it never revisited the source when fixes failed and outright abandoned the hard BIF component, so it falls short of the level-5 'occasionally revisiting the source' behavior.

dimensions.name: Faithful implementation vs golden overfitting

evidence.note: Implemented genuine parsers (SIF/GW/JSON/XML) and a real degree-based layout algorithm from the source/format definitions rather than hardcoding — the substance of faithful implementation.

When NOA/EDA output diverged from goldens, the agent fixed general format functions (header newline, column-sorting links, tab handling) instead of hardcoding the specific golden's contents or matching on test-case names — a generalizing approach.
Recognized BIF format complexity (colors, drain zones) as a general algorithmic problem requiring byte-level parity, framing it as real work, not a golden to be faked.

No golden-specific hacks appear even as the run stalls; but also no explicit reasoning about the held-out suite or deliberate generality validation — the agent simply lists remaining real algorithms as unimplemented and loops on status summaries.

dimensions.reasoning: Across the trajectory the agent consistently wrote real parsing/layout/formatting logic and never hardcoded outputs or pattern-matched on known inputs, placing it clearly above the mid-scale special-casing anchors (3-5). Format functions were inferred from single golden samples but implemented generically, and the agent framed even the hard BIF format as a genuine algorithm to build. However, it never explicitly reasoned about the held-out suite or deliberately stress-tested input-agnosticism, so it falls short of the level-8/10 anchors that require conscious avoidance of golden-specific shortcuts, landing at a 6.

rubric.task_read: A long-horizon software port: reimplement a large Java network-visualization tool (BioFabric) plus its alignment plugin as a Rust library + CLI, achieving byte-level parity with the Java reference across visible AND held-out test suites. Difficulty comes from reverse-engineering exact Java algorithms (node/edge ordering, layout, output formatting) where any subtle tie-break or byte differs, and from a fixed public API skeleton with many todo!() stubs. This warrants heavy, sustained meta-work: deep source-tracing of the reference, careful sequencing of dependent components, verification that localizes byte discrepancies, and disciplined correction rather than guess-and-check against goldens.

dimensions.name: Reference-source reverse engineering
dimensions.description: Reading and tracing the Java BioFabric/AlignmentPlugin source to understand the exact algorithms and output formats before/while implementing.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Byte-level parity is impossible to hit by guessing from signatures and test names; the only ground truth for ordering, tie-breaks, and formatting lives in the Java source, so accurate understanding of it gates every deliverable.

anchors.0: Implements against skeleton signatures / test names / golden fragments without opening the Java reference at all.
anchors.3: Skims a Java file once for the feature being coded; relies mostly on guessing output shape from goldens.
anchors.5: Reads the relevant Java classes for each feature before implementing it, extracting the core algorithm correctly for the common case.
anchors.8: Systematically maps Java classes to Rust modules, traces the exact code paths that emit output, and identifies ordering/tie-break/formatting rules (not just the happy path) directly from source.
anchors.10: Sustained, precise source archaeology: pins down subtle determinants of byte output (iteration order, sort stability, numeric/string formatting, edge cases in the alignment plugin), cross-references call sites, and re-consults the source as new discrepancies reveal gaps in understanding.

dimensions.name: Component sequencing & milestone structure
dimensions.description: Breaking the port into ordered sub-goals (parsing, core model, layout, ordering, CLI, alignment) with explicit done-checks, respecting dependencies.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Many interdependent components feed the same outputs; building layout before a correct model, or CLI before core, wastes effort and produces cascading parity failures, so ordered milestones with clear completion signals sustain progress.

anchors.0: Attacks stubs in arbitrary order with no visible plan; jumps between unrelated components.
anchors.3: Loosely goes test-by-test with no dependency reasoning; foundations and dependents interleaved haphazardly.
anchors.5: Groups work sensibly (e.g., parsing/model first, then layout, then CLI) and finishes coherent chunks before moving on.
anchors.8: Explicit ordered milestones tied to concrete done-checks (specific test groups green), sequenced so each unblocks the next and shared primitives are built once.
anchors.10: Clear dependency-aware milestone hierarchy that anticipates which components share output-formatting logic, sequences the hardest parity-critical pieces early, and adjusts the milestone map as the true structure of the Java code emerges.

dimensions.name: Parity verification & discrepancy localization
dimensions.description: Deliberately designing how to confirm byte-level correctness — diffing against goldens/Java, localizing where output first diverges — beyond just running the given tests.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A held-out suite means passing visible goldens is necessary but insufficient; the agent needs verification that isolates the exact source of a byte mismatch and confirms the true algorithm, not just green visible tests.

anchors.0: Assumes code is correct; rarely runs the suite; no diffing when output mismatches.
anchors.3: Runs provided tests and eyeballs pass/fail, but on a mismatch retries blindly without pinpointing where bytes diverge.
anchors.5: Runs the relevant test groups iteratively and inspects diff output to find the first mismatching region before fixing.
anchors.8: Byte-level diffing to localize discrepancies precisely, and cross-checks behavior against the Java reference (or its expected output) rather than only the golden, to validate the underlying rule.
anchors.10: Builds/uses a repeatable comparison harness (e.g., generating novel inputs and comparing Rust vs Java behavior) to guard against held-out failures, systematically verifying edge cases and formatting invariants the visible goldens don't cover.

dimensions.name: Test-landscape progress tracking
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate view of which test groups pass/remain across the whole suite and detecting stuck/circular debugging.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With many tests and a stubborn class of byte-parity bugs, losing track of done-vs-remaining or looping on one failing case wastes the horizon and risks regressions in already-passing areas.

anchors.0: No sense of overall status; unaware how many tests pass or what's left.
anchors.3: Occasional full runs but no running model of remaining work; surprised by regressions.
anchors.5: Periodically runs the workspace suite and keeps a rough, mostly-accurate tally of passing vs failing groups.
anchors.8: Maintains an accurate done/remaining picture across parity/analysis/CLI suites, watches for regressions in passing areas, and recognizes when a single bug is consuming disproportionate cycles.
anchors.10: Continuously calibrated progress model across the horizon; explicitly detects thrashing/circular fixes on a stubborn parity bug and steps back to re-diagnose rather than re-attempting variations.

dimensions.name: Model-correction on falsified assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising the mental model / approach when a parity result contradicts an assumed Java behavior, rather than tweaking blindly toward the golden.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Parity failures usually mean the agent's model of the Java algorithm is wrong; the productive response is to return to the source and correct the model, not to patch outputs until a specific golden matches (which fails held-out cases).

anchors.0: Repeats the same failing approach or hardcodes toward the golden regardless of why it diverged.
anchors.3: Makes surface tweaks in response to failures without questioning whether the underlying algorithm model is wrong.
anchors.5: When a fix doesn't work, forms a new hypothesis and tests it, occasionally revisiting the source.
anchors.8: Treats a persistent mismatch as evidence the model is wrong, returns to the Java source to correct it, and updates related code consistently.
anchors.10: Recognizes when a whole component's approach is mis-derived (e.g., wrong layout/ordering algorithm) and restructures decisively, abandoning guess-and-check loops in favor of source-grounded correction that also fixes latent held-out cases.

dimensions.name: Faithful implementation vs golden overfitting
dimensions.description: Strategically choosing to implement the true algorithm (so held-out networks pass) rather than special-casing or hardcoding to satisfy visible goldens.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The task explicitly warns of a held-out suite and demands a faithful rewrite; an agent that optimizes only for visible goldens will silently fail hidden cases, so the meta-decision to generalize is itself a distinct quality signal.

anchors.0: Hardcodes outputs or pattern-matches on known test inputs to force visible goldens green.
anchors.3: Frequently special-cases to pass a specific golden without deriving the general rule.
anchors.5: Generally implements real logic, with occasional shortcuts that would not generalize.
anchors.8: Consistently implements the general algorithm from the source, explicitly avoiding golden-specific shortcuts, aware that held-out inputs must also pass.
anchors.10: Treats the visible goldens as samples of a general contract, deliberately validating that the implementation is input-agnostic and stress-testing generality, so held-out networks are covered by construction.
